title: Three spectroscopically confirmed z≈6 quasars found through contrastive learning
summary: A self-supervised contrastive-learning search of Dark Energy Survey imaging isolated a group of 11 sources that included seven known z≈6 quasars. Follow-up Gemini-South and archival NTT spectroscopy confirmed three additional quasars at redshifts 5.94–6.07. One source, J0109−5424, shows evidence of a foreground object and is a lensed-quasar candidate, but its multiple-image status requires high-resolution imaging.
ai_technology: Self-supervised contrastive-learning neural network trained on Dark Energy Survey imaging data
organization: University of Cambridge; Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab; INAF; collaborators

evidence.tested: A self-supervised contrastive-learning search of Dark Energy Survey imaging isolated a group of 11 sources that included seven known z≈6 quasars.
evidence.unknown: The three quasar identifications are spectroscopically confirmed, but the possible gravitational lens interpretation of J0109−5424 remains unconfirmed pending high-resolution imaging. The reported 91% efficiency refers to ten quasars among the eleven-source island, including seven previously known objects; three of the four previously unclassified targets were confirmed quasars. It is not a universal completeness estimate.
evidence.ai_role: Grouped sources into a learned embedding-space island that prioritized four unclassified candidates; spectroscopy confirmed three as quasars, including one source missed by conventional color selection because foreground light contaminated the photometry.
